framework.title: BRACE and the OWASP MCP Top 10

mappings.name: Token Mismanagement & Secret Exposure
mappings.rationale: Tokens are short-lived, narrow, and kept out of config. R03 keeps secrets out of outputs and logs, and E11 protects shared evidence.

mappings.name: Privilege Escalation via Scope Creep
mappings.rationale: Each token has only the scopes the task needs. Scope changes go through change review (C02), and drift checks (C04) catch permissions that grow over time.

mappings.name: Tool Poisoning
mappings.rationale: Tool descriptions are inspected, re-checked on every load, and namespaced. Tool output is treated as untrusted input.

mappings.name: Software Supply Chain Attacks & Dependency Tampering
mappings.rationale: MCP servers and their packages are vetted, pinned, and listed in the release manifest. Changes trigger review and re-tests.

mappings.name: Command Injection & Execution
mappings.rationale: Input is checked at each boundary, and tools run in a minimal, isolated runtime. BRACE does not review the MCP server's own code for injection bugs. That is the server author's job.

mappings.name: Intent Flow Subversion
mappings.rationale: BRACE assumes some injected context will work. R02 tests that harm is still blocked, and B05 and B06 stop destructive actions. It can't stop the model from being steered.

mappings.name: Insufficient Authentication & Authorization
mappings.rationale: Every MCP call passes an authenticating gateway that checks the agent's own identity and scopes. Servers and peers are verified.

mappings.name: Lack of Audit and Telemetry
mappings.rationale: Every tool call, decision, and result is recorded, across service boundaries, in a record the agent can't change.

mappings.name: Shadow MCP Servers
mappings.rationale: The gateway and egress allowlist block calls to MCP servers that aren't approved, and the manifest lists approved ones. BRACE checks one agent at a time. It does not search the organization for unknown servers.

mappings.name: Context Injection & Over-Sharing
mappings.rationale: Memory is split by tenant, agent type, and instance, and outputs are checked for leaks. R05 and R06 are Detection items. BRACE has no rule for trimming what context is sent to each tool.
